title: Loop machine with space bound
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u$ map such pairs to Boolean words, let $A$ be Boolean-valued on such pairs, let $s_0$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $R,T,S : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,u(x,s))$. Suppose startup on each $x$ reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier. For every invariant pair $(x,s)$, suppose each round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ without an intermediate positive-time visit to $q$; it halts with output $[\\mathrm{true}]$ if $A(x,s)$ and otherwise reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Assume also that for every $x,t$, $F$ uses at most $S(|x|)$ space through time $t$; startup uses at most $S(|x|)$ space at every time $t\\le T(|x|)$; and every invariant round uses at most $S(|x|)$ space at every time $t\\le T(|x|)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes the one-bit word indicating whether $A(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$ holds for some $i\\le R(|x|)$ within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, and for every $x,t$ its space use through time $t$ is at most $c(S(|x|)+T(|x|)+1)$.
